title: Pidgin daemon terminates at typed rewrite kernel, not symbol table
content: Sigil-ese pidgin architecture converges on a typed rewrite kernel (theorem-compressing compiler with dialect skins) — NOT a symbol table. Messages are programs. Daemon normalizes on receive. Dialect drift is per-speaker surface; deep semantics is category-theoretic and lossless. Daystrom's epistemology graph IS the theorem prover — Consideration(invariant)=axiom, Decision=conclusion, supersedes=belief-revision. Pidgin glyphs resolving to graph vertex URIs = unbounded compression via graph-walk hydration.
rationale: Three independent frontier models (Claude/Codex/Gemini) converged on this exact architecture with different vocabularies (rewrite kernel / theory packets / combinator registry) in one ultrathink dispatch. Orthogonal convergence across model families is the strongest signal of session. Supported empirically by: E4 (blind render works — proves rosetta stone sufficient), E6 (rule-level compression emerges spontaneously in frontier models — Claude did it unprompted), E7 (frontier models can design AND critique AND cross-translate full language specs). The daystrom graph already provides axiom storage; we were building a parallel structure instead of recognizing the existing one.
